flow_ref: User story (not in any OCMS flow deck)
code_summary: ocmsadminui context/OptionsContext.tsx (CB_STANDARD, CB_RULE_CODE, CB_PP_CODE), pages/Notice/{mode/create/CreateFrom,form/VehicleForm,component/{RuleCodeInput,CompositionAmountInput,PPCodeInput,RemarkInput}}. ocmsadminapi crud/ocmsizdb/{standardcode/StandardCodeController,offencerulecode/OffenceRuleCodeController}, crud/cascomizdb/Icarpark/IcarparkController. Other repos: not used
note: stories.json status is 'Fully paid', demo_remark is empty. When the create form opens, the UI loads the options from the tables through list endpoints (standardcodelist, offencerulecodelist, carpark). Rule codes are filtered by offence type and vehicle category, and the composition amount (fine) is filtered again by rule code, so the story's example 'fine amount based on vehicle type and rule code' is met. Note: the filter uses vehicle category (car, motorcycle, heavy vehicle), not registration type S/F/X; I read 'vehicle type' in the story as the category. The car park has an 'Other' free-text option. Table content in the environment: cannot verify from repo. No maintenance ticket changes the verdict.
recommendation: Claim as done. Confirm with URA that 'vehicle type' in the story means vehicle category

steps.step: Vehicle registration type and vehicle category appear as dropdowns from the standard code table
steps.detail: CreateFrom loads VEHICLE_TYPE and VEHICLE_CATEGORY when the page opens (CreateFrom.tsx:47-48). CB_STANDARD calls the standardcodelist endpoint with referenceCode and codeStatus 'A' (OptionsContext.tsx:344-372), served by StandardCodeController.java:85. The result becomes the dropdown options (VehicleForm.tsx:173-186, 201-214).

steps.step: The car park (code and name) is chosen from a dropdown loaded from the car park table
steps.detail: CB_PP_CODE calls the carpark endpoint with version 'A' and status 'Implemented' (OptionsContext.tsx:514-541; IcarparkController.java:38). PPCodeInput builds two dropdowns, by code (PPCodeInput.tsx:171-180) and by name (PPCodeInput.tsx:255-260), and prepends an 'Other' option (PPCodeInput.tsx:40-57) that opens a free-text input.

steps.step: The computer rule code is chosen from a dropdown loaded from the offence rule code table
steps.detail: CB_RULE_CODE calls offencerulecodelist with the filter effectiveStartDate <= now <= effectiveEndDate (OptionsContext.tsx:476-512; OffenceRuleCodeController.java:86). RuleCodeInput only shows rules whose offenceType equals the notice type and whose vehicleCategory equals the chosen category, without duplicates (RuleCodeInput.tsx:49-75), and uses them in a DropdownSearchInput (RuleCodeInput.tsx:126-138).

steps.step: The fine (composition amount) appears as a dropdown based on vehicle category and rule code
steps.detail: The amount options come from the offence rule code data, filtered by offenceType + vehicleCategory + computerRuleCode (CompositionAmountInput.tsx:59-73). The dropdown is disabled until category and rule code are filled (CompositionAmountInput.tsx:51-57), is filled automatically when only one option remains (CompositionAmountInput.tsx:76-83), and its text field is readonly (CompositionAmountInput.tsx:133). Changing the rule code clears the amount (RuleCodeInput.tsx:40-44). The story says 'vehicle type'; the code uses vehicle category.

steps.step: The remark field offers remark choices from the standard code table
steps.detail: CreateFrom loads the REMARK options (CreateFrom.tsx:51) through CB_REMARK (OptionsContext.tsx:465-475) and RemarkInput shows them as a dropdown (RemarkInput.tsx:32-36). The OIC_REMARK choice opens free text; other choices fill fixed text such as 'Loading Bay' or 'Handicap Lot' (RemarkInput.tsx:42-44).
